content.text: I feel like I'm missing something here, so I probably am, but what is malformed about that SPARQL? Certainly, it's not what you intended to send, but there's nothing actually invalid about it, is there? How would Fedora know to reject it?
Since the underlying error comes from:
java.net.URI.create(URI.java:852)
..Fedora should be verifying the provided namespace is a valid URI before inserting it into the namespace-registry:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-kernel-modeshape/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/kernel/modeshape/rdf/converters/PropertyConverter.java#L153-L155

I guess you are right that "malformed" is probably the wrong way to put it.  Somebody could legitimately have a URI with hash character that was not intended to delimit a fragment, but TBL calls that "unsafe" (see
http://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc1738.txt)
Unsafe:
Characters can be unsafe for a number of reasons.  The space
character is unsafe because significant spaces may disappear and
insignificant spaces may be introduced when URLs are transcribed or
typeset or subjected to the treatment of word-processing programs.
The characters "<" and ">" are unsafe because they are used as the
delimiters around URLs in free text; the quote mark (""") is used to
delimit URLs in some systems.  The character "#" is unsafe and should
always be encoded because it is used in World Wide Web and in other
systems to delimit a URL from a fragment/anchor identifier that might
follow it.  The character "%" is unsafe because it is used for
encodings of other characters.  Other characters are unsafe because
gateways and other transport agents are known to sometimes modify
such characters....
So I don't really know what position Fedora should take on users choosing to be unsafe, but it does seem as though the object should not become unretrievable if somebody does this.
Yeah,
, I didn't mean to imply that there's no problem here, just trying to characterize it carefully. It's not possible for Fedora to DWIM here, but it is possible for it to DWIS, which it currently is
not
doing.
The underlying problem here is that Fedora is trying to do namespace management. There is no reason to do that here. But fixing that is way more effort than it is worth.
Personally, I'm becoming increasingly fond of completely separating the Fedora implementation from the namespace management. There is no inherent need for the two to be so closely tied together.
Do you have a pattern in mind for how to externalize the namespace management,
+1 to Fedora not managing namespaces.
There is no pattern needed. Namespaces just get treated as document-scoped, URIs internally are full (no prefixes used). Done.
What

said: basically, the implementation stores full URIs. Namespaces are only needed for RDF serialization, and they can be pulled in at that point, using a simple file, a database or anything, for that matter, capable of
get
and
put
. But at this point, we're talking about something very different that the current Modeshape-based implementation.
, fyi, it is helpful if you can add a link as a comment in JIRA to your PR.

Please comment on or merge this PR into your branch.
Resolved with:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/cd4433c7ed3e161f1376afc48b0087f67db37f64
It is possible to cause non-RDFsource objects to "disappear" from the repository with a malformed SPARQL query.  Steps to reproduce:
1. upload a binary object, for example to
http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/test
2. PATCH the metadata on this node with the following SPARQL (note the erroneous double hash-mark character in the PCDM URI):

url -ufedoraAdmin:secret3 -X PATCH -H "Content-Type: application/sparql-update" --data "INSERT DATA {<> <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type> <http://pcdm.org/models##file> .}" "http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/test/fcr:metadata"
3. Fedora returns a Java stack trace on subsequent accesses to the /fcr:metadata, or 404 not found errors for the nonRDF node.  The exact behavior varies from browser to browser.

I would expect fedora to catch the SPARQL syntax error before saving the malformed triple on the node, and it does seem to do this for other similar errors, but for whatever reason this one slips through and causes the resource to become unreachable.
observed in fcrepo4-vagrant
